issue.title: Follow-up search query absorbs names from GAIA's own wrong answer
issue.symptom: 8xr4.20 builds a follow-up query from the question plus the proper nouns of the last assistant turn. When that answer was wrong, its names steer the next search: 'Who threw it back into the lake when he died? Excalibur sword Arthur Merlin Malory's Le Morte Pellinore' (from a confabulated 'Pellinore' answer) found TV Tropes / Merlin wiki, not Bedivere. Prefer user-turn subject words; take assistant names only if they also appear in earlier grounding results.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/tests/test_knowledge_followup.py
"""8xr4.20: "Where did he get the sword?" after Excalibur was filed as chat, so
nothing grounded it, and Stage 0 web-searched {'ENTITY': 'he', 'PLACE':
'sword'} verbatim (Onimusha, katana prints, Roblox codes). Follow-ups now take
their search query from the whole exchange, and Stage 0 drops subject-less
entities and spends at most one web search per turn."""

import json
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest

from gaia_core.cognition import knowledge_router
from gaia_core.cognition.agent_core import _clean_grounding_entities
from gaia_core.cognition.nlu import intent_detection
from gaia_core.cognition.nlu.intent_detection import is_knowledge_followup

HIST = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Can you tell me the name of King Arthur's sword?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "The name of King Arthur's sword is Excalibur."},
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    "Where did he get the sword?",
    "And who gave it to him?",
    "What happened to it after he died?",
    "So when did they find it?",
    "Which knight returned it to the lake?",  # "it"
])


def test_followup_context_keeps_recurring_names_and_drops_one_answer_particulars():
    ctx = knowledge_router.followup_context(WRONG_ANSWER_WINDOW)
    q = knowledge_router.followup_query("Who threw it back into the lake when he died?", ctx)
    assert "Excalibur" in q and "Arthur" in q
    for particular in ("Pellinore", "Merlin", "Malory"):
        assert particular not in q
    assert ctx[1] == "Where did he get the sword?"  # user turns verbatim


def test_followup_context_falls_back_to_the_answer_when_nothing_else_names_the_subject():
    ctx = knowledge_router.followup_context([
        {"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about the sword in the stone."},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "That would be Excalibur, in most tellings."},
    ])
    assert ctx == ["Tell me about the sword in the stone.", "Excalibur"]


def test_followup_context_user_named_subject_needs_no_answer_names():
    # "Excalibur" said once is not needed: the user's "King Arthur's sword"
    # finds the same pages (checked live, 2026-10-28).
    ctx = knowledge_router.followup_context(HIST)
    assert ctx[0] == HIST[0]["content"] and "King" in ctx[1] and "Excalibur" not in ctx[1]


def test_followup_context_strips_answers_first():
    ctx = knowledge_router.followup_context(
        [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about the sword."},
         {"role": "assistant", "content": "<think>Merlin?</think>Excalibur."}],
        strip=lambda t: t.split("</think>")[-1])
    assert ctx[1] == "Excalibur"

+def followup_context(turns: List[Dict[str, Any]], strip=lambda t: t) -> List[str]:
+    """Context for a follow-up's search query, from the recent turns: the
+    user's turns as they were, and from GAIA's answers only the names the
+    conversation returns to — said in at least two of these turns, by
+    either side. Those name the subject ("Excalibur", "Arthur"); a name
+    said once is a particular of one answer, possibly a wrong one (2vei:
+    a confabulated "…Merlin … Malory's Le Morte … Pellinore" answer sent
+    "Who threw it back into the lake?" to Pellinore pages; with only the
+    subject names the top result was Bedivere). When the user's turns name
+    nothing and no name recurs, the latest answer is the only subject
+    available, so its names are used.
+
+    `strip` cleans an answer's text (think tags, mind tag) first.
+    """
+    texts = [(t.get("role"), (t.get("content") or "") if t.get("role") == "user"
+              else strip(t.get("content") or "")) for t in turns
+             if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("role") in ("user", "assistant")]
+    turn_names = [{_name_key(w) for w in proper_nouns(text).split()} for _, text in texts]
+    seen_in = {}
+    for names in turn_names:
+        for n in names:
+            seen_in[n] = seen_in.get(n, 0) + 1
+    user_named = any(names for (role, _), names in zip(texts, turn_names) if role == "user")
+    context: List[str] = []
+    recurring_any = False
+    for (role, text), names in zip(texts, turn_names):
+        if role == "user":
+            context.append(text)
+            continue
+        keep = [w for w in proper_nouns(text).split() if seen_in.get(_name_key(w), 0) >= 2]
+        recurring_any = recurring_any or bool(keep)
+        context.append(" ".join(keep))
+    if not user_named and not recurring_any:
+        for i in range(len(texts) - 1, -1, -1):
+            if texts[i][0] == "assistant":
+                context[i] = proper_nouns(texts[i][1])
+                break
+    return context
